1.name: Base
1.note: A wooden plinth that carries the whole engine and keeps the hot parts clear of the bench.

2.name: Crankcase
2.note: The casting that carries the gear shafts and cylinder, and holds the drive in line.

3.name: Wood screw
3.note: Four screws that fix the crankcase to the base.

4.name: Spur gear
4.note: Two meshing gears with the same tooth count. They turn in opposite directions at the same speed, which keeps the rhombic drive balanced.

5.name: Gear shaft
5.note: Carries a gear and a crank pin, and turns in the crankcase.

6.name: Crank pin
6.note: Offset 9 mm from the gear axis, it turns the rotation into the stroke of the connecting rods.

7.name: Connecting rod
7.note: Four rods form the rhombus. Two push the piston yoke, two the displacer yoke, in opposite directions.

8.name: Yoke pin
8.note: Joins each connecting rod to its yoke.

9.name: Piston yoke
9.note: The cross-piece the two upper rods push together. It moves the piston rod straight up and down.

10.name: Displacer yoke
10.note: The lower cross-piece, which moves the displacer rod. Its phase against the piston is what makes the cycle work.

11.name: Piston rod tube
11.note: A hollow rod from the piston yoke to the piston. The displacer rod slides inside it.

12.name: Displacer rod
12.note: Passes through the piston and links the displacer yoke to the displacer.

13.name: Power piston
13.note: The piston the pressure swing pushes on. It is where the engine takes its work.

14.name: Piston ring
14.note: Seals the piston in the liner without oil, so the sealed charge of air stays in.

15.name: Rod bushing
15.note: A bronze guide and seal for the displacer rod where it passes through the piston rod tube.

16.name: Cylinder liner
16.note: The wall the piston slides in. Cast iron is hard-wearing against the PTFE rings.

17.name: Cooler cylinder
17.note: A finned aluminium jacket that carries heat out of the gas to the air. It is the cold end of the engine.

18.name: Cap screw
18.note: Ten screws clamp the cooler, gasket and hot cap together.

19.name: Gasket
19.note: Seals the hot joint between cooler and cap. Graphite takes the heat.

20.name: Hot cap
20.note: The dome the burner heats. It is the hot space of the sealed charge.

21.name: Displacer
21.note: A thin hollow plunger that shuttles the air between hot cap and cooler. The 1 mm gap round it is the regenerator.

22.name: Heat shield
22.note: Keeps the burner's heat off the cooler, so the temperature difference is kept up.

23.name: Burner ring
23.note: A ring of 12 jets that spreads the flame round the hot cap. Turning the burner down shrinks the P–V loop.

24.name: Flywheel
24.note: Stores energy from the power stroke and carries the engine through the rest of the cycle.

25.name: Hex nut
25.note: Locks the flywheel on its shaft.
